Inspiration

It All Started with Trollface

The faces in this gallery were born from the long tradition of the most legendary hand-drawn meme on the internet.

  1. 2008

    Drawn in MS Paint

    Trollface was first drawn by Carlos Ramirez (aka Whynne) in MS Paint and uploaded to DeviantArt on September 19, 2008 — originally to mock people who were "trolling" but failing miserably at it.

  2. 2009

    The Rage Comic Era

    The face exploded through 4-panel comics made by Reddit and 4chan users. A whole family of rage faces was born: Trollface, Rage Guy, Me Gusta, Forever Alone, all the way to Poker Face — every one of them a deliberately "ugly" hand-drawn black-and-white face.

  3. 2010s

    A Universal Language

    Trollface's grin needs no translation. One image reads the same everywhere: "I just pranked you." The format spread to stickers, t-shirts, and chat reaction emojis.

  4. Now

    A New Take on the LOL Face

    The collection on this page redraws that same spirit — a round chubby face, thick ink lines, wavy cheeks — and expands it into twenty expressions: laughing, cheeky, angry, crying, shocked, deadpan, winking, sleepy, in love, cool, a blank one ready for captions — plus a second wave of variants and a brand-new panic face.

01

Bold, Rough Lines

Thick black outlines with messy, uneven strokes are the signature. The "drawn in a hurry in Paint" look is the aesthetic, not a flaw.

02

Exaggerated Expressions

Mouths stretched as wide as they go, eyes squeezed shut and wrinkled, cheeks pushed up high. The more over-the-top the expression, the faster the message lands.

03

Black & White Only

No color, no complicated shading. Ink-on-white-paper contrast keeps the face perfectly readable even at tiny sticker size.

04

Motion Lines on the Cheeks

Small curves around the cheeks make the face feel like it's shaking — laughing, holding back emotion, or trembling. A small detail with a big effect.
